page: OVHcloud c2-30-flex is a compute-oriented virtual server instance powered by KVM virtualization. The configuration provides 8 dedicated x86_64 physical cores running on 3.0 GHz Intel Haswell architecture processors without hyperthreading. Cache structures comprise 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB shared L3 cache. Memory capacity totals 30.0 GB of RAM, offering 3.75 GB per core. The instance includes 50 GB of local SSD storage and features no discrete hardware GPU accelerators. The baseline network speed is reported at 0 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are bundled.

Benchmark results place the instance consistently within the middle 50 percent tier across standard compute and memory metrics. The instance achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1217.0 and a multi-core score of 6140.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 13178.87 and stress-ng multi-core throughput of 12121.28. In application-specific testing, software compilation using Clang scores 11388.0, and static web serving throughput reaches 9.41 GB/sec. Large-block uncached memory transfers measure 70.08 GB/sec for read operations and 42.22 GB/sec for write operations, supporting in-memory workloads such as Redis SET operations at 12.97 million operations per second.

Hardware tradeoffs stem largely from the older Haswell microarchitecture. The CPU supports AVX, FMA, AES, and BMI2 instruction sets, but lacks newer extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX. This limitation is evident in modern machine learning workloads, where 7B parameter LLM inference falls into the bottom 25 percent tier at 23.68 tokens per second for prompt processing and 8.62 tokens per second for generation. Furthermore, local storage is restricted to 50 GB SSD space, requiring network storage attachment for data-heavy operations.

The qualitative cost profile is driven by dedicated core execution and balanced memory allocation without the overhead of modern vector accelerators or bundled GPU hardware. OVHcloud c2-30-flex fits intermediate compute workloads, software build servers, continuous integration pipelines, web application hosting, and moderate in-memory key-value stores.
